scope: Independent read-only security and release-decision audit. No fresh business execution. Release artifacts excluded.

controller_security_execution.runner_semantics: Java main serializes case results; outer Python runner returns nonzero when any case security assertion fails. A successful Java process does not establish passing security behavior.
controller_security_execution.initial_failure: Mockito attachment failed before assertions; subclass mock maker permitted final execution.

sec01.setup: Synthetic user owns expired access and an unexpired correctly signed refresh credential for one session identifier. RSA verification and actual controller/session logic execute.
steps: Observe HTTP-style controller response and revocation repository.
Submit the same valid refresh credential to relogin.
Assert replay rejection and absence of new access.
sec01.expected: Completed logout revokes this session; subsequent relogin returns 401 and issues no access.
sec01.source_cause: logout calls retrieveUserInfoFromToken, which validates expiry before extracting the session identifier. Expired access throws before sessionService.create. The catch logs and continues to success. relogin accepts a valid refresh when no revoked session record exists.
sec01.origin: INHERITED_BFF_DEFECT; inspected baseline and current control flow validate expiry before revocation and still report success.
sec01.baseline_comparison: security-review.json records matching control flow ignoring logs and whitespace; independently inspected exact baseline and candidate controller source.
sec01.priority: P1 conditional analyst proposal retained from existing security review.
sec01.severity_proposal: High / S2 conditional analyst rating; serious continued-authentication exposure when another party holds a copied valid refresh. No official organizational severity policy was found.
sec01.severity_limits: No credential theft, unauthorized business action, financial loss, target exposure, or production frequency was demonstrated. A critical S1 rating would need broader supported consequence or policy.
sec01.user_impact: A user can believe logout ended their session while a holder of the copied refresh can regain authenticated access as that user until refresh expiry or another effective revocation. Protected business access after issuance was not exercised.
sec01.acceptability_advice: NOT_ACCEPTABLE_FOR_POSITIVE_SECURITY_OR_RELEASE_RECOMMENDATION on the matching source composition. Inherited origin is not an accepted waiver. Correct revocation or prove the release path is not applicable with a reviewed effective mitigation, then reassess.
sec01.next_action: Use a reviewed authenticated revocation path without trusting unverified JWT payloads. Verify expired-access logout, refresh replay, valid-access control, browser flow, and replica behavior.
sec01.closure_evidence: Matching server and browser evidence must show the same-session refresh rejected after logout, with no issued access. Preserve rejection of forged credentials and actual policy scope.
sec01.confidence: HIGH for declared isolated path; production applicability UNKNOWN
limits: Actual controller/JWT/session-service classes; repository and entitlement dependencies mocked. Servlet requests and responses mocked.
No HTTP server, browser, live provider, production, or multi-replica verification.
Frontend clears its local credentials, but local clearing cannot revoke a copied refresh credential.

recommended_scoped_decision.controlling_dimension: SEC-01 server revocation 5/5 FAILED. Direct current source-bound execution proves the local material failure.
recommended_scoped_decision.score_basis: 20 times lowest controlling score 5. This is certainty in the source-composition hold, not completeness, deployment applicability, readiness, or incident probability.
recommended_scoped_decision.remaining_gaps: Full current-source unit execution, browser supported caller, broad unrun cases, target transports and unresolved policy remain visible. They cannot offset the demonstrated failure.
recommended_scoped_decision.alternative_if_scope_excludes_bff: A frontend-only impact assessment could isolate the inherited BFF defect as an external residual risk. That exclusion must be explicit and source-backed; do not silently inherit the user's P4 backlog decision for this newly found P1 security issue.
